walkthroughs.body_html:
Three families of process matter.

Weathering breaks rocks where they sit.

Erosion removes pieces; mass movement slides them downslope.

Freeze-thaw is common in UK uplands.

Water seeps into cracks, freezes overnight and expands ~9%.

Repeated cycles split rock and build scree slopes.

People are now huge agents of change.

Farming clears woodland; quarrying carves hillsides; cities pave floodplains.

Some changes happen in decades, far faster than nature.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between glacial abrasion and plucking?
options: Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
Abrasion: rock embedded in the glacier base scrapes the bedrock smooth, creating striations. Plucking: meltwater refreezes onto bedrock, then movement rips chunks of rock away.
Abrasion is when wind erodes the glacier and plucking is when rain does.
Abrasion and plucking are different words for the same process.

mcqs.q: How do glaciers form U-shaped valleys?
options: U-shaped valleys form when rivers freeze and expand.
Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
Glaciers carve U-shaped valleys from flat land by pushing through.
Glaciers erode existing V-shaped river valleys through plucking (freezing onto rock and pulling pieces away) and abrasion (rock embedded in the ice scraping the valley floor and sides).

mcqs.q: What drives the movement of tectonic plates?
options: Abrasion is when wind erodes the glacier and plucking is when rain does.
Convection currents in the mantle combined with slab pull at subduction zones and ridge push at constructive boundaries.
Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
The Earth's rotation makes the plates move.
